reviewer: Pickle: burn time-temperature thresholds, foot-bath water temperature regulation and recalls, diabetic foot-care cautions, foot-bath circulatory and sleep evidence, mould and dermatophyte survival, KEPCO tariff calculation, and Coupang/Kakao product terms
method: Reviewed the draft against the 23 recorded facts and 22 listed citations on 2026-11-13. Burn time-temperature: the Plumbing Manufacturers Institute table reproducing Moritz and Henriques (Am J Pathol 1947) gives 44 C at 4.5 h and 5 h, 45 C at 2 h and 3 h, 47 C at 20 min and 45 min, 48 C at 15 min and 20 min, 49 C at 8 min and 10 min, 52 C at 45 s and 1.5 min, 55 C at 17 s and 30 s, and 60 C at 3 s and 5 s, so the article lists these as first- and second-degree burn times. NASA OCHMO-TB-009 puts pain onset at 43 C, tissue damage at 49 C, and about 8 minutes to third-degree injury at 49 C. Water temperature rule: the Electrical Appliances and Consumer Products Safety Control Act limits water in contact with skin to no more than 45 C; the 2020 National Institute of Technology and Standards recall measured the Vitagram WGT-1230 foot bath at 47.8 to 48.7 C and the Hutopia HT-2057A at 45.9 to 46.1 C, and the Gudfriend GOOD-F14 heating pad stone at 92.5 C against a 60 C limit, as reported by Dong-A Ilbo from the NITS and KCA release. KCA 2018: the Nadi Happybody BM-202 exceeded 45 C with the bubble function off, sales stopped, and 493 units sold from 2017-11-16 to 2018-04-04 were repaired free, per SR Times. KCA 2005: of 25 electric foot baths the maximum water temperature ranged from 43 to 60 C with 8 products above 50 C, and among 79 foot-bath complaints leakage was 31.7 percent and burns or electric shock 19.0 percent, per Water Journal. KCA 2020 electric blanket analysis: 902 cases in 2017 to 2019, second-degree burns 63.1 percent (391 of 620), buttocks and legs and feet 68.4 percent (503 of 735), winter 48.5 percent. FTC and KCA 2022 appliance warning: 3,244 heat-appliance cases from 2018 to 2021, 514 burns, 66 heating-pad injuries, and low-temperature burns defined as 42 to 43 C for more than one hour. Diabetes: the Korean Diabetes Association foot-care page says not to wash feet in hot water, not to soak them long, and not to use heating devices in direct contact with the feet because of sensory loss; KDCA diabetic foot guidance says neuropathy hides pain and temperature and advises checking foot-bath water with a hand or thermometer, with about 50 percent of neuropathy asymptomatic per the KDA guideline. The German diabinfo portal recommends a 37 to 38 C foot bath for 3 to 5 minutes. Foot-bath physiology: Xu and Uebaba (2003) tested 38, 40 and 42 C baths for 30 minutes in 14 women and propose 20 to 25 minutes at 38 C, 15 minutes at 40 C and 10 minutes at 42 C, noting raised pulsatility index at 42 C; Liao et al. (2008) found a raised distal-proximal gradient but no significant sleep change at 41 C for 40 minutes; the 2025 meta-analysis of 6 RCTs and 176 participants found no statistically significant sleep benefit. Cold extremities: the family-medicine study reports a 12 percent prevalence of cold hands and feet, Raynaud 5 to 10 percent, up to 25 percent in young women, and a female-to-male ratio of 2.3, with a local column citing 5-fold female predominance. Hinoki: the 2023 forest-recreation study of 46 students inhaling Chamaecyparis obtusa oil for 90 seconds reported higher HF and lower tension and depression; the Korea Forest Service southern office release attributes a halving of blood cortisol to hinoki phytoncide. Mould and dermatophytes: Tsongas and Riordan give 80 percent RH for germination and 85 percent for visible growth; Lee et al. found dermatophytes in 33 of 70 slippers (47.1 percent) and Essien et al. give D80 values of 3.2 to 4.4 minutes, so a 45 to 55 C soak does not sterilise. Electricity: KEPCO residential low-voltage rates of 120.0, 214.6 and 307.3 won per kWh plus 9 won climate and 5 won fuel adjustment, with 10 percent VAT and a 2.7 percent fund levy, give about 258 won per kWh in the second tier; 160 W for 30 minutes a day for 30 days is 2.4 kWh and about 619 won, and 400 W on the same schedule is 6 kWh and about 1,549 won, with the 400 W wet-bath figure stated as an assumption because wattage varies by product. Products: the three Coupang listings were opened in the browser on 2026-11-13. OA Bubblefoot OMS-024WH at 42,540 won after 47 percent off 80,550 won with 217 reviews at 4.5, more than 300 buyers in a month and a 40,830 won lowest third-party price, with massage, remote, heating and timer listed and the water temperature not stated on the page. Gudfriend GOOD-F40 at 134,500 won after coupon from 149,000 won, 114,430 won lowest third-party price, 117 reviews at 5.0, 160 W, 3.5 kg, 30 to 65 C and 1 to 99 minutes from reviews, 8 ceramic stones, removable velcro cover, hinoki and hemlock per reviews, with the seller Q&A on a sibling model stating a carbon heater rather than far-infrared. Vitagram VG-FB1000 at 39,900 won with 750 reviews at 4.5 and no drain per the seller answer. Zespa ZP5443 at 48,150 won after 56 percent off 110,000 won with 285 reviews at 4.5, three levels each of air pressure, heat and vibration, USB-C, 15-minute auto stop and up to 4 hours per charge, with the lining not removable. Kakao Gift: curator link Ikbi1yUL was created on 2026-11-13 for the Slroom wireless calf heat roller massager at 36,900 won from 89,000 won, 30,510 won best price, 382 gift reviews at 4.0, over 10,000 wishes, 3,321 won expected commission, electrical safety certification and free standard shipping with a 5,000 won surcharge for Jeju and islands, and the required curator disclosure appears in the article. Coupang deep links were built from the pageKey, itemId and vendorItemId read on each product page and each returned a 302 to the matching product. Gate score 100/100 with 250 of 250 numbers backed by the research file.
